successors.name: Shaishunaga dynasty
successors.text: Asmaka on the Godavari with Mulaka; infobox 'Succeeded by: Magadha'

ledger.x: c. 600 BCE: Asmaka, the only Mahajanapada of the Deccan, is ruled from Potali on the Godavari. 'Ashmaka (or Assaka) was the only Mahajanapada located in South India'; infobox 'c. 700 BCE' established, 'Capital: Potali, also called Podana, Paudanyapura, or Potana', 'Most scholars identify it with present-day Bodhan in…
Mid-6th century BCE (undated): Asmaka annexes Mulaka to its west.

c. 345 BCE: Asmaka passes to Magadha. Infobox 'Disestablished 425 or 345 BCE', 'Succeeded by: Magadha'; the page names no conqueror and no campaign. The Cliopatria row alive in -345 is the Shaishunaga dynasty (-404..-334); the Mahajanapadas page has 'The Nandas usurped the throne of Shishunaga dynasty c. 345 BCE', so…

wars.name: Kalinga's invasion of Assaka
wars.outcome: In a Jataka tale the Kalinga king invaded Assaka and was defeated through diplomacy; he 'was forced to send a portion of his daughters' dowry to Assaka' and the two kings kept peaceful relations.

wars.name: Asmaka's annexation of Mulaka
wars.outcome: Mulaka annexed by Asmaka 'during the Mahajanapada period'; Asmaka 'became the southern neighbour of the kingdom of Avanti'.

certainty.note: The Godavari is the only line the pages give (it 'separated the country of the Assakas from that of the Mulakas' before the annexation); every other edge is a radius.
